record.title: China sets out a central policy to link scientific research with industrial innovation
record.summary: A joint Central Committee General Office and State Council opinion published by China’s Ministry of Science and Technology calls for closer integration of scientific research and industrial development. It directs stronger enterprise roles in national science programs and commercialization, a pilot opening of National Natural Science Foundation programs to private firms, greater access for companies to major research infrastructure, instruments and national scientific-data centers, stronger R&D incentives for technology SMEs, and “AI+” deployment across industries. The opinion also identifies embodied intelligence among future-industry fields. The document states policy directions; it gives no funding amounts, named program calls, implementation results or measured effects.

State Council of the People’s Republic of China
Ministry of Science and Technology of the People’s Republic of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A joint Central Committee General Office and State Council opinion dated and published 2026-10-21 directs closer integration of research and industrial innovation, with enterprises taking a stronger role in national science programs, commercialization and research collaboration.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The text calls for a pilot opening of National Natural Science Foundation programs to private enterprises; wider enterprise access to major scientific infrastructure, large research instruments and national scientific-data centers; stronger R&D incentives for technology SMEs; and “AI+” implementation across industries.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The opinion states high-level policy directions. This source does not specify the pilot’s eligibility or funding amount, a quantified tax rate, operational access rules, named beneficiaries, or realized research or industrial outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The opinion does not specify how the private-enterprise funding pilot or increased access to public infrastructure/data will operate, nor what funding or capacity will be committed.
No implementation or outcome evidence accompanies the opinion; effects on AI research, SME innovation or industrial productivity are unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, a central national framework making firms active leaders in research programming and opening major public scientific resources to enterprise use could influence research funding, commercialization and AI-industrialization pathways. The policy has broad reach, but no budget, implementation record or outcome is established here.
limitations: The source establishes the published central policy direction, not implementation.
No funding allocation, eligibility rule, quantified tax adjustment, facility-access protocol, beneficiary list or measured outcome is specified in this document.
The use of “AI+” and embodied intelligence is a policy priority signal; it is not proof of new model, compute or robotics program resources.

technical.claimed_result: The opinion says these measures are intended to improve coordination of scientific and industrial innovation and support high-quality technology development. These are stated policy aims rather than measured effects.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official ministry page provides the dated full original Chinese opinion and directly states the listed policy directions. It is evidence of the policy text, not evidence that programs, budgets or access changes have been implemented.
technical.mechanism: A whole-of-government framework coordinates science and industrial policy through enterprise participation in program design and review, industry-led applied project organization, commercialization incentives, access to public science infrastructure and data, SME R&D incentives, research-industry collaboration and AI+ deployment. It also lists embodied intelligence among future-industry fields.
technical.novelty: The opinion places research-program governance, firm access to public science assets, commercialization, finance and AI industrialization within a single central policy framework. The novelty claim is limited to the published policy package; implementation is not demonstrated.
technical.regime: China national science, industrial and innovation policy as stated in a central opinion issued by the Central Committee General Office and State Council and published on the Ministry of Science and Technology site on 2026-10-21. No implementation date, budget or outcome is established by this document.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable: this is a government policy document, not a measured technical or economic comparison.

brief.title: China sets out a central policy to link scientific research with industrial innovation
brief.why_it_matters: If implemented, the opinion could change how Chinese research priorities, public research assets and innovation finance connect to firms, including AI-related industries. Its significance is institutional: it links enterprise-led R&D, research commercialization, access to public science infrastructure and AI industrialization in one central policy framework. The policy text alone does not show what resources will be committed or whether access and incentives will change in practice.

related.summary: The Oct 21 national innovation-industry opinion overlaps in enterprise R&D and commercialization but is a separate policy event.

other.title: Reports describe a Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei science-finance implementation plan
other.summary: Two reports dated Oct 21 state that Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei financial and science authorities released a regional implementation plan at the Oct 20 Financial Street Forum. They describe a six-part, 15-measure package spanning long-term capital, research and technology-transfer loans, cross-region financial services, technology insurance and cross-border finance. This development records the reported policy announcement on Oct 21; the signed plan was not recovered, and the reports provide no funding allocation, uptake or outcome evidence.

other.title: China issues multi-agency finance guideline for three science and technology hubs
other.summary: A guideline dated 19 October and published by China's Ministry of Science and Technology the next day was jointly issued by 11 central agencies to support finance for innovation hubs in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. It sets 2030 and 2035 goals and directs central-local science funding, regional venture-capital funds, patient capital, a relending pilot for R&D-intensive private SMEs, cross-region finance and data coordination, technology-transfer finance, bond support and selected cross-border services. Regional authorities are asked to prepare implementation rules. The document establishes policy directions, not committed amounts, implementation, capital uptake or economic outcomes.
